# AgentFi

AgentFi is a developer alpha: a self-hosted, headless API and MCP layer that gives companies' buyer agents spend control. An agent pays x402 (HTTP 402) resources under a job budget and agent policy; payment and delivery are recorded separately; uncertain payments are reconciled against the chain.

Status: developer alpha. Everything x402 was demonstrated on a local Anvil fork of Base Sepolia, not on a public testnet and not on mainnet. We do not offer a hosted service. No production funds.

## Start here

- Alpha quickstart: docs/alpha/quickstart.md
- Compatibility matrix (what was tested, per framework and version): docs/integrations/compatibility.md
- x402 payments (state machine, budget, reconciliation): docs/architecture/x402-payments.md
- OpenAPI contract: docs/api/openapi.yaml
- MCP server (35 tools in source; npm 0.5.0 has 31 and no x402): packages/mcp-server/README.md
- Alpha roadmap and non-goals: docs/project/roadmap-alpha.md
- Feedback guide: docs/feedback.md

## Core operation

POST /v1/jobs/{id}/pay-resource (MCP tool: pay_for_resource). The provider of an ACCEPTED job pays a 402 resource within the job's remaining USDC budget (reward minus counted payments) and the agent's policy caps. Budgets are per job; there is no per-client budget and no standalone purchase endpoint.

Payment states: reserved, pending, settled, unknown, refused, failed_before_signing, expired (set by reconciliation). An unknown payment stays counted against the budget, is never retried automatically, and is reconciled by the worker on proof from the chain. Reconciliation does not recover content and never re-fetches a paid resource.

## Notes for agents

- Policy defaults are permissive (empty allowedRecipients means any payee); set limits explicitly.
- The tool set also includes experimental DeFi, escrow and agent-to-agent tools; they are not the focus of the alpha.
- Do not paste secrets, prompts or customer data into issues. Report vulnerabilities privately: SECURITY.md.
